host.note: Reconstructed session: the replies were written by an agent playing this session; every embed was computed by the host from the graphs named.

turns.request: The mechanical consultant sent over analytics_dataset_with_levels.csv — carbon and energy numbers for the Duplex, keyed by GlobalId. Can you open it and tell me what's in it?
turns.reply: 268 rows, columns GlobalId, Name, Level, operational_carbon, energy_intensity, category. The key column is GlobalId, the same 22-character id the model itself uses, so nothing needs remapping before a join.

turns.request: Join it to the Duplex model on GlobalId, against the physical elements only, and tell me what matched.
turns.reply: 216 of the model's 237 physical elements (entities with a rendered mesh) match a row in the file. 21 physical elements have no row; 52 file rows match an entity that exists but is not itself physical — mostly the opening behind a door or window rather than the door or window. Both counts are reported, not dropped.

turns.request: Which physical elements did the file miss?
turns.reply: All 21 are IfcSpace — Living Room, Kitchen, two Bathrooms, two Bedrooms, Hallway, Foyer, Utility, Stair, Room, Roof — one mesh per room, the space boundary itself. The consultant's file only has rows for building elements, not rooms, so this gap is the file's scope, not a mismatch.

embeds.caption: Physical elements with no file row

turns.request: And the file rows that don't line up with anything physical?
turns.reply: 52 rows. 50 are keyed to the opening behind a door or window (IfcOpeningElement), not the door or window mesh itself; 2 are keyed to a stair that is meshed only through its flights, never as one entity. The file's numbers for these rows still exist — they just have nowhere to land as a colour yet.

embeds.caption: File rows with no physical element

turns.request: Colour the model by operational carbon from the file, and grey out anything it doesn't reach.
turns.reply: Viridis gradient from 14.2 to 412.0 kgCO2e/yr. 693 of the model's 714 mesh instances take a colour; the 21 instances behind the rooms from two turns ago stay grey, exactly the elements the match report already named.

turns.request: This is going to happen again with the next consultant's file. Can we save it so someone else just points it at their own model and spreadsheet?
turns.reply: Saved as a template. Three groups of parameters carry a new model and file without touching the shape of the joins: the file's path on `csv`, plus the join column name repeated on `matched`, `unmatchedInModel`, `unmatchedInFile`, and `coloredCarbon` if the new file spells its key column differently; the model's path on `model`, plus the source name on `entities` if a different model's database is used. Point those at the next consultant's spreadsheet and model, and the match report and the colouring above update the same way.
